figures.caption: Fig. 1: Proposed neuromorphic SiLIF-DBS controller. The input current Isyn is integrated by Cmem to generate VMEM, with M1 providing leak control through VLEAK. The threshold stage (M3,M4) compares VMEM with VTH to produce VCOMP, which is converted into the spike output SOUT by INV1 and INV2. The reset and refractory branch (M2,M7,M10,CRF) generates VREFN using VRF.
Fig. 2: Hardware–software equivalence of the SiLIF-DBS controller at 150 Hz for VRF = 0.26 V.
Fig. 3: Relationship between refractory voltage, VRF and DBS frequency of the SiLIF-DBS controller.
Fig. 4: Illustration of integration of SiLIF-DBS controller into the PD computational model.
TABLE II: Matching parameters for the circuit design and computational model of the SiLIF-DBS controller.
Fig. 5: Raw STN-LFP and beta-band filtered STN-LFP for biomarker characterization.
Fig. 6: Power spectral density (PSD) of raw STN LFP and beta-band filtered STN-LFP.
Fig. 7: Output of the SiLIF-DBS controller with Beta ARV as input: (a) Raw STN-LFP, (b) Beta-band filtered STNLFP, (c) Beta ARV, and (d) Adaptive DBS of the SiLIF-DBS controller.

Fig. 8: Neuromorphic SiLIF-DBS suppresses pathological beta activity in the Parkinsonian model. (a) Beta-band (13–30 Hz) filtered STN local field potentials (LFPs) comparing DBS Off and SiLIF-DBS conditions. (b) Beta average rectified value (Beta ARV) of the filtered LFP.
Fig. 9: Energy Efficiency of SiLIF-DBS Compared to Conventional Controllers.
